points.description: States that the frequency of light is proportional to its energy (higher frequency means higher energy photon).
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if the link is implied, e.g. 'higher frequency = more energy' without the word proportional.

points.description: States that the energy levels of an electron in an atom are quantized (only certain, discrete energies are allowed).

Explains that the energy (and so frequency) of light absorbed to excite an electron between levels must equal the difference between two allowed energy levels, so only certain frequencies are absorbed.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if it says only specific frequencies work because of energy levels but does not say the absorbed energy must equal the level difference.

points.description: States that a minimum amount of energy (threshold energy, set by the binding of the electron) is needed to eject an electron from the atom.
States that any energy above the minimum is transferred to the ejected electron as kinetic energy, so any frequency above the threshold is absorbed.
points.partial_credit: 1 mark if it says the extra energy goes to the electron but does not name kinetic energy or explain why any value is allowed.

rubric.notes: Full marks need all five ideas: frequency is proportional to photon energy; electron energy levels are quantized; absorbed energy must equal the gap between two levels (so only certain frequencies work); ejection needs a minimum threshold energy; and any excess energy becomes the electron's kinetic energy (so any higher frequency works). Give half marks for a claim that is clearly there but only partly stated, as described in the partial credit column. A correct explanation worded informally counts in full. Blank, off-topic, or generic restatement of the question (for example, just saying light has energy) earns nothing. Wrong extra remarks do not cost marks unless they contradict the central idea of a point.
